cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is about to die. Before his death, Moses the man of God speaks a blessing over the Israelites. It's his last big speech, friend, and the man spends it blessing everybody else.
Before he blesses a single tribe, Moses starts with the LORD showing up for His people. The LORD came from Sinai, dawned from Seir and shone forth from Mount Paran.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD came with myriads of holy ones. What does Moses say is at His right hand?

cards.text: Then Moses talks right to the LORD and says it plain: Surely You love the people. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, I would have CRIED at "Surely You remember the stamper."

cards.question: Moses says the holy ones sit at the LORD's feet, and each one receives His words. Those words are the ___ that Moses gave us.
Moses says the LORD became King in Jeshurun when the tribes of Israel came together.
Now Moses blesses the tribes one by one, starting with the tribe of Reuben. Moses says Reuben's men will be few.

cards.text: Next up, the tribe of Judah. Moses asks the LORD to hear the cry of Judah and bring him to his people.

cards.question: Judah defends his cause with his own hands. Moses asks the LORD to be his ___ against his foes.

cards.text: Then the tribe of Levi. Moses asks the LORD to give His Thummim and His Urim to Levi, His godly one.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD tested Levi and contested him at the waters. Where did that happen?

cards.text: Then Moses says Levi said of his father and mother, "I do not consider them." He disregarded his brothers and didn't even know his own sons.

cards.question: Moses says Levi disregarded his brothers and didn't know his own sons. Why?

answers.text: He kept God's word and covenant
He wanted a bigger share of land
He was angry with his brothers

cards.question: Moses says Levi will teach the LORD's ordinances to Jacob and His law to Israel.

cards.text: Levi will serve at the altar too, and Moses asks the LORD to bless his substance and accept the work of his hands. Teaching AND the altar, friend, and I can't run ONE oven without singeing my mustache.

cards.question: Next is the tribe of Benjamin. Moses calls him the beloved of the LORD, shielded by God all day long. Moses says Benjamin rests upon the LORD's ___.

cards.text: Then the tribe of Joseph, and Moses goes BIG: may his land be blessed with dew from heaven, deep waters below, the harvest from the sun and the best of the ancient mountains. That's not a blessing, friend, that's a whole TOPPING BAR.

cards.question: On top of all that, Moses names someone's favor to rest on Joseph's head. Whose favor is it?

answers.text: Him who dwelt in the burning bush
The king who ruled over Egypt
The elders who sat at the gate

cards.question: Moses says Joseph's majesty is like a strong animal. Which one?
Moses says Joseph will gore the nations. Such are the myriads of ___ and the thousands of ___.

cards.text: Now Moses blesses the tribes of Zebulun and Issachar together. Rejoice, Zebulun, in your journeys, he says, and Issachar, in your tents.

cards.question: Moses says Zebulun and Issachar will call the peoples to a mountain. What will they offer there?
Moses says Zebulun and Issachar will feast on the abundance of the seas.

cards.text: Next is the tribe of Gad, and Moses says blessed is he who enlarges the domain of Gad. Friend, the only domain I ever enlarged was the flour cloud around my counter.

cards.question: Moses says Gad lies down like a ___ and tears off an arm or a head.
Moses says Gad chose the best land and came with the leaders of the people. What did Gad carry out for Israel?
The tribe of Dan gets the shortest blessing yet. Moses calls Dan a lion's cub leaping out of Bashan.

cards.text: Then the tribe of Naphtali. Moses says Naphtali is abounding with favor, full of the blessing of the LORD.

cards.question: Moses says Naphtali will take possession of the mountains and the north.

cards.text: Last tribe on the list: Asher. Moses says, May Asher be the most blessed of sons, the most favored among his brothers.

cards.question: Moses wants Asher to be so blessed that he can dip his foot in ___.

cards.text: I once dipped my whole gold base in cookie dough, and NOBODY called that a blessing. Then Moses says, May the bolts of your gate be iron and bronze.

cards.question: Moses ends Asher's blessing by wanting Asher's strength to match his ___.

cards.text: Then Moses is done naming tribes, and he comes back to the LORD. There is none like the God of Jeshurun, he says, who rides the heavens to your aid.

cards.question: Moses says the eternal God is Israel's dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting ___.

cards.text: In the junk drawer, friend, all I had underneath me was a stack of old takeout menus. Israel gets the everlasting arms, and a God who drives out the enemy before them.

cards.question: With God driving out the enemy, Moses pictures Israel in a land of grain and new wine. How does he say Israel dwells there?
Moses ends with a shout: Blessed are you, O Israel, who is like you? What does Moses call Israel?

answers.text: A people saved by the LORD

cards.question: Moses says the LORD is the shield that protects Israel and the sword they boast in.

cards.text: Their enemies will cower before them, Moses says. And that's where the blessing ends, friend, but trust me, Moses' story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess a detail of the picture (what is at the LORD's right hand: flaming fire, a golden scepter or a shepherd's staff). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward fire. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example of guessing what David's head is anointed with.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "song" is arguable. Moses gave Israel a song just before this (Deut 31:22; 32), and that song comes earlier in this same story group. A baker could argue that "the song that Moses gave us" fits.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the last word of the line ('upon His ___ he rests'). Shoulders, altar and throne can't be told apart by reasoning. The card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess which animal Joseph's majesty is compared to (bull, eagle or stallion). This is a detail guess, the same as the Psalm 23 bad example, and the setup gives nothing to reason from.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Ephraim and Manasseh appear for the first time with no word on who they are (Joseph's sons, whose tribes come from Joseph). On top of that, the two blanks make the baker guess which name goes with 'myriads' and which with 'thousands'. That is pure wording order, not meaning.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Once the baker knows the names, the only thing left to get right is the order of Ephraim and Manasseh in the line. That tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks what animal Gad lies down like (lion, bear or wolf). This is a detail and wording guess with nothing in the setup to reason from.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'So blessed that he can dip his foot in' adds a cause-and-effect link the text doesn't make. Deut 33:24 lists 'most favored among his brothers and dip his foot in oil' side by side.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Guessing what Asher dips his foot in (oil, water or honey) is the same detail guess as the Psalm 23 bad example of what David's head is anointed with (oil, myrrh or perfume).

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line 'may your strength match your ___' (days, brothers or enemies). That is wording the baker hasn't seen and can't reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line 'underneath are the everlasting ___' (arms, stones or roots). That is guessing the next word of a line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Too many choice cards across both stops are detail or wording guesses that need luck (S1 cards 3, 16, 19 and 20; S2 cards 5, 11, 13 and 15). That is far more than 'a few' discovery questions, so most choice cards here are not informed guesses about movement and meaning.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
